answer: One $120 TPM chip seals each agent identity, its endorsement key a quill sealed in silicon. A new identity must finish a voyage past three rotating verifier checkpoints, each stamping the key after a hardware challenge. No epoch takes more than five identities from one batch, so identical-chip farms hit a dune wall. 100 clones need 100 chips at $120 plus $40 provisioning each, scarce batches lifting the average to $235, a $23,500 bill against $160 for one honest agent. One failed check burns the whole batch. A copied quill is useless without its chip, like a passport without its traveler.
